content.text:
**Finding: deviation (high severity) — § 7.2 (first of two clauses numbered 7.2), p0026.**

- **What's wrong:** "Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives." This binds *us*, not Vendor, and functions as an open-ended right of first refusal on our sourcing — no product-category limit, no 12-month sunset, and no automatic exit on Vendor's service-level or delivery failure. It therefore fails the fallback position and approaches walk-away exclusive dealing.
- **Internal inconsistency:** § 12.3 (p0044) has Vendor acknowledging that Customer has made "no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment," which squarely contradicts § 7.2.
- **Redline (validated, preferred level):** replaces the match obligation with express non-exclusivity — Vendor is a non-exclusive provider and we may engage any other provider without notice or any duty to disclose or match. The fallback (defined category, 12 months, performance-based exit) is offered in the comment.
- Flagged only once: this is treated as a sourcing restraint under EXCLUSIVITY, independent of any pricing/MFN analysis.
